Sequential validation steps from raw capture to clinical grading.
Fundus capture intake and initial format checks
Illumination, focus, and field centration filter
Complete Retinal Field: Optic disc, macula, and major vascular arcades must be visibly centered.
Sharp Focus: Vascular bifurcations should be crisp. Avoid motion blur or out-of-focus captures.
Balanced Illumination: Ensure uniform illumination. Avoid high-glare flash reflections or dark under-exposed frames.
Avoid Obstructions: Ensure eyelashes, eyelid margins, and pupil-edge vignetting do not occlude the retina.
Clinical Note: Passing dimension and format checks does not guarantee diagnostic suitability. Final quality is verified by the NetraProof Optical Quality Assessment Model in Stage 02.
Architecture: Five-fold EfficientNet-B0 ensemble with ordinal regression.
Predicts one of five ICDR diabetic retinopathy severity tiers: Grade 0 (No DR), Grade 1 (Mild NPDR), Grade 2 (Moderate NPDR), Grade 3 (Severe NPDR), and Grade 4 (Proliferative DR).
Generates pixel-level lesion overlays across 4 key biomarker classes: Microaneurysms, Hemorrhages, Hard Exudates, and Cotton Wool Spots.
Architectural Rule: The grading model and segmentation model operate independently. Lesion segmentation provides visual evidence and is NOT proof of the grading prediction.
NetraProof AI is an assistive medical technology tool and does not replace an eye examination by an ophthalmologist.
